purpose: The Cloud owner processes a conforming installation runs, and the environment each process requires.
machineBoundary: Cloud declares the owner processes, their addresses, databases and peer identities. The instance owner selects the provider, supplies the domain, Secrets and certificates, and performs deployment. This contract declares the owner topology's environment names and their roles. The environment template declares the values an installation provides, once each: a name this contract lists is a name the template declares, a name the host provides, a name the Compose files derive from one of those, or a build argument. No fact is declared with a value in both places.

image.fact: One product image carries every owner executable; the installation selects which processes to run.

derivedEnv.peerTokensShape: JSON object {"<peer owner identity>":"<at least 32 characters>"}

distinctAddressesEvidence: The declared listen address of an owner is the address the published portable installation binds for it, and that installation binds a distinct address for every owner, so no two owners share a port in one Pod/network namespace. The installation admission resolves an absent listen environment to the Product-declared defaultAddress (Fabric defaultRPCAddress); an explicit nonempty listen env overrides that default and must match the Service targetPort. The owners' own sources keep the fallback they bind when no listen environment is declared: the Ledger and the Resource Catalog sources both fall back to ":8186", and the Fabric and the Gateway Integration sources both fall back to ":8187". Those shared fallbacks conflict only when sharing one Pod/network namespace; Separate Deployments may use the same declared default listen port. The Serve access entry falls back to ":8188".

notes: Package/WebUI/build-result catalog owner. OPL_CAPABILITY_STORAGE_KIND selects the object store; the COS_* set is required only for the object-store kind.
Runs the admitted BuildKit build; OPL_BUILD_BUILDER and OPL_BUILD_WORKDIR are installation facts for the build host.
Owns Runtime Release admission and immutable release readback. It never owns a running instance.
Owns the accepted order and resource intent; it persists no second current-deployment pointer.

Reads purchase eligibility from its single retained Control Plane owner through typed HTTP using OPL_CONTROL_PLANE_URL and the independent OPL_CONTROL_PLANE_WORKSPACE_TOKEN shared by both processes. This read adds no writer and is outside the gRPC communication edges.

Sole writer of default-App and Agent deployment/readiness/access facts, and the owner of the Workspace route binding and its access data plane. OPL_SERVE_ACCESS_ADDR names the application entry Serve serves itself; OPL_PUBLIC_URL, OPL_WORKSPACE_DOMAIN and OPL_WORKSPACE_APPLICATION_DOMAIN are the installation's declared route origin for that entry. No installation route provider is configured by any environment variable: the route object is Serve's own access binding.

Serve owns application execution. A TKE installation declares its namespace, kubeconfig Secret reference, image-pull Secret, credential seed, the ingress peers allowed to reach a Workspace application, and the same protected-compute facts Fabric's provider is bounded by; Serve then applies, observes, scales and retires the workload itself.

OPL_FABRIC_APPLICATION_URL with its service token and capability key remains only for the provider whose in-process executor has not moved yet. An installation that declares both OPL_K8S_NAMESPACE and OPL_FABRIC_APPLICATION_URL is refused at startup, because that would be two writers for one workload.
The legacy LEDGER_ADDR spelling is still read for the retained HTTP surface.
OPL_POSTGRES_TESTS only selects the isolated database harness; production never sets it.

CloudIdentity/Tenant and Gateway Integration share one process, but remain distinct database and writer owners. DATABASE_URL opens Tenant; OPL_GATEWAY_DATABASE_URL is required and opens the separate Gateway database. Missing OPL_GATEWAY_DATABASE_URL aborts startup; startup migrates the Gateway database and includes it in readiness checks.
Owns infrastructure resource mutation and readback only. The legacy signed HTTP application-runtime surface is the migration bridge that I06 retires.
Migration source, not a permanent second writer; it also serves the Console static bundle.

Cloud announcement reads use the authenticated BFF-only typed HTTP boundary; Control Plane revalidates its Cloud session with Gateway under the control_plane transport principal and retains publication/ACK persistence.

Remains the single purchase-eligibility owner, serving Workspace through typed HTTP with OPL_CONTROL_PLANE_WORKSPACE_TOKEN independently of BFF and outbound credentials; this adds no writer. Either BFF or Workspace token activates its CloudIdentity client.

The BFF owns no business data and holds no database. It reaches each owner through OPL_<OWNER>_URL/OPL_<OWNER>_TOKEN, while an owner process listens on OPL_<OWNER>_ADDR and admits callers through OPL_<OWNER>_PEER_TOKENS: an installation must set both spellings for the same target.

deploymentUnit.rule: The Cloud backend is one deployment unit: one container in which the owner processes this contract already declares run together in one process space. Domain ownership does not require a separate process, container, Kubernetes Deployment or network hop, so this declaration names no member of its own: the members are exactly the processes this contract already declares and the image is the one this contract already declares. The unit reaches a small declared set of dependencies that are not processes of its own, and it deliberately leaves privileged build execution and customer Workspace application execution outside itself. An instance owner keeps installation configuration, Secrets, deployment, rollback and receipts; this declaration states only what the product's own unit contains, reaches and excludes.

unit.name: opl-cloud-backend
unit.memberRule: Every process this contract declares is a member of this unit. This block adds no member and removes none, so the contract keeps one writer of the member list.
unit.boundaryEffect: A restart or an upgrade of this unit restarts every member. A workload that must not share that boundary is an exclusion, not a member.

readinessCriteria.rule: Every declared process carries exactly one readiness criterion: the check an installation runs to decide whether the process is ready to serve, and the check that decides whether it is only alive. A criterion names the process it belongs to, its kind, and the concrete checks it makes. Every check names the transport it uses, whether it answers the readiness question or the liveness question, and the address environment name this contract already declares for that process, whether that is the process's own listen address or one of its additional listeners. A criterion therefore never introduces an address of its own: the effective address resolves from the same declaration the process reads. A gRPC check is the owner's own health service; an HTTP check is a route the owning source registers. A check marked as a projection reports another owner's readiness state rather than an aggregate of Cloud owners, and names the Go type its body carries. Cloud declares no aggregate readiness surface: /readyz belongs to the Ledger owner alone.

externalConsumers.rule: A route that only a consumer in another repository calls stays registered while that consumer calls it. This declaration owns that fact: the route exists for a named consumer outside this repository, not because a Cloud repository happens to call it. Every declared path must be a route the Control Plane registers, so a Cloud change cannot silently drop a surface another repository still uses.

evidence: The declaration owns the Cloud route, not the survival of its call sites. workspace-launch-stage-observation.mjs is being retired in a separate Instance PR; the other three call sites stay. The route stays registered while the Instance installation still reads it, so the number of call sites is not the test for whether the surface is still needed.

browserApiSurface.requirement: The Console is served from one origin and calls both browser-facing surfaces, so a browser-facing installation routes /api/ to control-plane and /api/v2/ to console-bff on the same public host. An installation that routes only one of them serves a Console whose other half cannot answer. Every route on a browser facing surface names a client in the owning source: a Console call site, an operator tool, one of the installation probes declared here, or a consumer in another repository declared under externalConsumers.

communication.scope: Current owner gRPC transports only; retained signed HTTP and object-store transports are separate contracts.
communication.principals: caller and target are transport principals. gateway resolves to tenant in the gateway-integration deployment unit; console_bff is a transport principal, not a business owner.
communication.activation: required edges apply when the caller RPC surface is installed. configured edges retain address-or-token admission: address activation and the dialed address value follow that edge's configuredAddressSemantics (raw-nonempty or trimmed-nonempty using Go strings.TrimSpace); token and activationEnvs activation always use Go strings.TrimSpace. Unresolved references cannot disable a potentially configured edge. rpcEnabledByEnvSemantics separately declares optional process RPC activation: Ledger uses raw-nonempty; Fabric uses trimmed-nonempty. Listener defaulting is separate from activation. An unrelated env/optionalEnv entry is never made mandatory by this contract.
communication.deploymentIdentity: An explicit Kubernetes command plus args must exactly match the process binary followed by daemonArgs. Absent/empty command and args use defaultCommand only for a proven Product image. An args-only override cannot prove the inherited image entrypoint. Probe and unsupported argv cannot prove a daemon. Deployment names and labels are installation facts, never service-name heuristics.

peerAddresses.scope: The caller-side environments the published installation sets on an owner to reach another owner, and the target owner's own declared listener each one names. The gRPC peer graph is declared by communication.edges; this block declares the retained HTTP peer origins that graph does not carry, so every environment the installation uses to reach a peer is declared exactly once and never twice.
peerAddresses.principals: caller and target are transport principals, the same identities communication.edges uses: gateway resolves to tenant in the gateway-integration deployment unit, and console_bff and control_plane are transport principals rather than business owners.
peerAddresses.binding: targetAddressEnv names the target owner's own declared listen environment, and originScheme names the scheme the peer origin uses; it is one of the schemes this block declares in originSchemes. The port a consumer must reach is that owner's declared listener port, read from the target's own process declaration; this block restates no port and names no host. An installation that runs the owners in one network namespace resolves a peer through this declaration: it takes the target's own effective listener address, keeps the declared scheme and effective listener port, converts a wildcard listener host to its matching loopback interface, and preserves an explicitly bound listener host. Nothing is invented and no port is restated.
peerAddresses.activation: configured entries apply when the caller's environment carries a value, following that entry's configuredAddressSemantics. The edge graph keeps its own required and configured admission rules; this block never relaxes them.
